RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

An all-male panel is not evidence of bias on its own — in economics, panels like that are common simply because the field's senior ranks are male-dominated. It's context, not proof, and leading with it will make you look like you're reaching.

Your stronger facts are the credential gap (completed PhD vs. unfinished, six papers vs. two) and the unanswered request for written reasons. Push those. Repeat the request in writing, citing the university's own procedures and any statutory right to reasons, and ask for the scoring criteria and how each candidate was ranked.

If the criteria were vague, invented late, or weighted to "industry experience" only after shortlisting, that's where a real case lives. Mention panel composition then — as pattern, not accusation.
